finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into the SQL string with an f-string. An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run UNION SELECT queries to read any table in shop.db, such as user or credential tables. They can also alter the query's logic.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes attacker input with no validation
term is interpolated directly into the SQL text and executed
Query results are returned as JSON, so UNION-based data exfiltration is visible to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on the route. No input validation, escaping or allowlist. No parameterized query. The /product and /by-owner routes use ? placeholders, but this one does not. No WAF or middleware in the file.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q unvalidated and app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL f-string with no auth, parameterization or allowlist, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so UNION exfiltration is possible; sqlite3 execute() accepts only one statement, which limits stacked queries but not UNION.
